title: Silas and the Letter
premise: In 1898, Marguerite Quintana, a pearl diver's son indentured to the Voss Trading Company, has spent his life making himself small and useful, measuring everything by what can be carried when the orders come. When the seasonal bridge closes and he is trapped in the company town with a dying letter-writer, Silas, who once forged documents to free indentured divers, Marguerite must choose between finishing Silas's final letters — including one that could expose the company's debt fraud — and obeying the ship that will carry him away on the morning tide. As the workshop is threatened with demolition, Marguerite learns to write in his own hand, falls into a forbidden love with the harbormaster's daughter, and finally delivers the letters himself. The book ends with him staying behind as the ship sails without him, the workshop burned but the truth carried across the bridge when it reopens.
about_author: P. M. Eriksen is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trading-company ledgers from the late colonial pearl fisheries. This is their second novel, drawn from a single unsigned letter found sewn into an indenture book.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. He inventories his life in portable things: a mother's shell comb, a diver's knife, his indenture papers. Establishes the Voss compound, the closed bridge, and his philosophy of invisibility. Emotional beat: quiet resignation mistaken for contentment.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wrote Other People's Names
chapters.summary: Marguerite is sent to deliver ink to Silas Okafor, the aging letter-writer whose cramped shop sits at the edge of company land. Silas recognizes Marguerite's father's name in an old ledger and says too much. POV alternates. Beat: first crack in Marguerite's safe smallness.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: The company announces the season's last shipment; all indentured hands must board the morning-tide ship or forfeit their contracts. Marguerite's POV. He begins packing before the order is finished speaking. Beat: dread dressed up as duty.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Storm damage closes the only road out early; the ship will wait at anchor, but the town is sealed. Silas's POV reveals he is dying and has unfinished work: letters of manumission for divers still held past their terms. Beat: the trap becomes a door.

chapters.title: Apprentice by Accident
chapters.summary: Marguerite, needing shelter from a company audit, hides in Silas's shop and is caught copying a hand that isn't his own. Silas offers to teach him properly. Marguerite's POV. Beat: reluctant fascination with a skill he was never meant to have.

chapters.title: Ink and Salt
chapters.summary: Lessons begin. Silas teaches not just penmanship but how names are made and unmade on paper. Flashbacks to Marguerite's father, erased from the ledgers after a diving death. Marguerite's POV. Beat: grief given a language.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Daughter
chapters.summary: Adelise catches Marguerite smuggling paper past the quay and, instead of reporting him, asks him to forge a passage chit — for her own escape. Her POV. Beat: two people recognizing each other's cages.

chapters.title: The Ledger With Two Truths
chapters.summary: Marguerite discovers the company keeps duplicate ledgers; debts are inflated so no indenture ever ends. Silas admits he has copied the true one for years. Marguerite's POV. Beat: outrage arriving late and cold.

chapters.title: A Letter in His Father's Hand
chapters.summary: Silas shows Marguerite a manumission letter signed with his father's name — written after the drowning, to free his mother, never delivered. Marguerite's POV. Beat: fury at Silas, then at himself for wanting to leave anyway.

chapters.title: The Inspector
chapters.summary: Company inspector Brandt arrives ahead of the demolition order for the waterfront shops, sniffing for the leaked ledger. Silas's POV; his cough worsens. Beat: the clock starts ticking in earnest.

chapters.title: Chit for Two
chapters.summary: Adelise and Marguerite meet at night; forging her chit becomes something closer to a promise. She asks what he'll do if he stays. He can't answer. Alternating POV. Beat: love against duty, named aloud for the first time.

chapters.title: The Workshop Still Stands
chapters.summary: Demolition notices posted; the shop has weeks. Silas, failing fast, makes Marguerite swear to finish the remaining eleven letters before the tide. Marguerite's POV. Beat: an oath taken half-willingly.

chapters.title: Hands That Aren't Mine
chapters.summary: Marguerite forges his first full letter — a manumission for a diver named Okon — and hates how easily his hand obeys. Silas argues that a borrowed hand can still carry true weight. Marguerite's POV. Beat: crisis of identity through craft.

chapters.title: Brandt's Offer
chapters.summary: Brandt corners Marguerite: betray Silas and board the ship with a clean contract and a bonus. Marguerite's POV. He says yes. Beat: the lowest point disguised as prudence.

chapters.title: What My Mother Carried
chapters.summary: Marguerite visits his mother, who gives him the shell comb and tells him she always knew who wrote the undelivered letter. Her forgiveness reframes his betrayal of Silas. Mother's brief POV, mostly his. Beat: shame turned toward repair.

chapters.title: Silas Fails
chapters.summary: Silas collapses mid-letter; Marguerite finishes it alone, in Silas's hand, perfectly — and realizes he no longer needs the disguise. Silas dies at dawn asking only that the letters travel by human hand, not post. Marguerite's POV. Beat: inheritance of a burden.

chapters.title: Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Marguerite works through the night list of names, Adelise keeping watch and forging the harbor pass. They plan delivery during the boarding chaos. Alternating POV. Beat: love expressed as complicity.

chapters.title: Fire Before Tide
chapters.summary: Brandt, suspicious, orders the shop burned early. Marguerite saves the true ledger and the letters, losing everything else, watched by half the town who say nothing. His POV. Beat: the town chooses its side silently.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Boarding day. Marguerite stands at the gangplank with his packed bag — everything he can carry — while Adelise distributes the letters among departing divers' families. Climax beat: the choice between the ship and the work made physical.

chapters.title: Stay Invisible No Longer
chapters.summary: Marguerite steps back from the plank and publicly signs his own name to the ledger copy, handing it to a departing delegate to carry over the bridge when it opens. Brandt moves to seize him; the crowd closes around. His POV. Beat: climax — justice outside the law, witnessed.

chapters.title: After the Ship Sails
chapters.summary: The ship leaves without him. Consequences arrive: charges, questions, Adelise's father's rage. But the divers' families begin reading names aloud from delivered letters. Marguerite's POV. Beat: cost counted honestly, worth affirmed.

chapters.title: A Hand of His Own
chapters.summary: Spring; the bridge reopens. Marguerite, awaiting trial, opens a small writing stand in the ashes' footprint and writes his mother's manumission in his own hand at last. Adelise brings him paper. Final beat: identity claimed, love chosen, the work finished.
